text: Police can swab your DNA at booking because the Supreme Court called it identification. That word does not mean what you think it means.
provenance: In 2013, by a single vote, the Supreme Court said they are allowed to do that.

text: Fingerprints are allowed at booking for one reason. Their purpose is confirming that the person in the cell is who they say they are.
provenance: Courts have long allowed this, because its purpose is identification — confirming that the person in the cell is who they say they are, and checking whether they are wanted elsewhere

text: Justice Kennedy said identification meant more than a name. Knowing an arrestee's full history helps officers judge how dangerous he might be.
provenance: Kennedy also spelled out what "identification" meant to the majority, and it was broader than a name.
Knowing an arrestee's full history, the Court said, helps officers judge how dangerous he might be, whether he is a flight risk, and whether he threatens the people around him.

text: Whether he is a flight risk. Whether he threatens the people around him. On that reading the swab was not a fishing expedition. It was processing.
provenance: DNA, in that view, was not a fishing expedition — it was part of safely processing a person already in the state's custody

text: The database has a name, CODIS, the FBI's national DNA index. The whole value of swabbing arrestees comes from searching it against cold cases.
provenance: CODIS, the FBI's national DNA index

text: Scalia answered that the police already knew who King was. The purpose was investigating unsolved crimes, which the Constitution forbids without suspicion.
provenance: The swab, he said, was not really about identifying Alonzo King
Its purpose was to investigate unsolved crimes, and the Constitution does not allow the government to search a person for evidence of crime without a reason to suspect them of it

text: He warned that a person's DNA can be taken and entered into a national database if they are ever arrested, rightly or wrongly.
provenance: as a consequence of this decision, he wrote, your DNA can be taken and entered into a national DNA database if you are ever arrested, rightly or wrongly, and for whatever reason

text: The four in dissent lost, which means the definition in the majority opinion is the one police work from today.
